articles.title: To Debate in 2028, Democrats Will Have to Disavow Dark Money
articles.summary: The Democratic National Committee (DNC) on Monday announced plans for 12 debates in the 2028 Democratic presidential primary, beginning in June 2027. The framework, released earlier than usual, includes a new requirement: To qualify for the debates, candidates must sign a pledge to denounce certain outside spending. Candidates will need to sign the newly released Fair Campaign Practices Pledge, denouncing both super PAC spending and “dark money,” which is any political funding from undisclosed sources. articles.title: What to Know About The Supermoon Appearing This Thanksgiving Week
articles.summary: There will be a lot of things competing for your attention this Thanksgiving week: the travel, the turkey , the family, the football. But spare a moment for the sky. On Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday, Nov. 23 to 25, a spectacular full moon known as a supermoon will shine overhead, visible both in the evening and, though not as dazzlingly, during the day. articles.title: Will Bad Weather Disrupt Thanksgiving Travel?
articles.summary: Millions are expected to travel this week ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday, but stormy weather and coastal flooding in parts of the country could disrupt plans during one of the year’s busiest travel periods. AAA projects 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home for Thanksgiving between Tuesday, Nov. 24 and Monday, Nov. 30. articles.title: 6 Questions About Jensen Huang's Stunning Return as Nvidia CEO
articles.summary: Eleven days. That’s how long it took Jensen Huang to return to his post of CEO of Nvidia after resigning in the wake of an alleged espionage scandal that rocked the business, tech, and policy worlds. On Nov. 12, Huang stepped down from the company he co-founded in 1993 after acknowledging an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese national whom U.S. intelligence officials reportedly suspected was a Chinese spy.
